candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record explicitly states that maxillary exostosis was only the initial diagnostic hypothesis, and histopathological analysis was required to establish the final diagnosis. Peripheral odontoma (the reference) is an odontogenic tumor/hamartoma, while maxillary exostosis is a non-odontogenic bony protuberance. The two share anatomical location and calcified appearance but represent incompatible diagnostic categories with different tissue composition and etiology.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Maxillary exostosis is a reactive bony outgrowth of cortical bone, whereas peripheral odontoma is an odontogenic hamartoma composed of dental hard tissues; both can present as calcified anterior maxillary masses but are distinct diagnostic entities
